dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a natural number n, this is the type of real n-by-n matrices, represented as functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes G a square real matrix whose row and column indices both range over Fin n.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real n-by-n matrix A, this is sqrt(sum_i sum_j (A i j)^2), with both sums over all indices in Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the matrix quantity in the hypothesis, namely the Frobenius norm of G.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a matrix A and vector x, this is the matrix-vector product Matrix.mulVec A x.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the vector in the left-hand side of the conclusion equal to G a.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real vector x indexed by Fin n, this is sqrt(sum_i (x i)^2).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the Euclidean norm used for both G a and a.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite index type with n indices, conventionally represented by natural numbers strictly less than n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It indexes all rows, columns, and vector coordinates and therefore fixes every dimension at n.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the multiplication operation supplied by an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real instances, it interprets the right-hand side as the ordinary real product epsilon * LocalDef004 a.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the binary less-than-or-equal relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With Real.instLE, both displayed relations are ordinary inequalities between real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The dimension n is universally quantified over all natural numbers, including zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Matrix entries, vector coordinates, epsilon, norms, sums, and products are all real-valued.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips Real with its standard order relation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns the hypothesis and conclusion into standard real inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips Real with ordinary real multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the multiplication epsilon * ||a||_2 and contributes the multiplication used in matrix-vector products and squares.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a multiplication operation on a type, this constructs homogeneous multiplication HMul alpha alpha alpha using that operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It connects HMul.hMul in the conclusion to ordinary multiplication on Real.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies a finite enumeration of every element of Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the coordinate, row, and column sums finite sums over all n indices.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: This sums the values of a function over a finite set using the additive commutative monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the sums of squared entries, squared coordinates, and the finite dot products in matrix-vector multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite type, this is the finite set containing every element of that type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures that every norm-defining sum ranges over every index in Fin n.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the exponentiation operation supplied by an HPow instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets each occurrence of an entry or coordinate raised to 2 as its real square.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix
dependency_coverage.meaning: A matrix with row type m, column type n, and entries in alpha is a function m -> n -> alpha.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the pointwise interpretation G i j of the real square matrix G.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.mulVec
dependency_coverage.meaning: For each row index i, matrix-vector multiplication returns the dot product of row j |-> M i j with v, namely sum_j M i j * v j.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Thus the i-th coordinate of LocalDef003 G a is sum_j G i j * a j.

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: A monoid supplies natural-number exponentiation by repeated multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the real natural power operation used to form every square x^2.

dependency_coverage.name: NonUnitalCommRing.toNonUnitalNonAssocCommRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: This forgets part of a nonunital commutative ring structure while retaining the nonunital, potentially nonassociative commutative ring operations.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is part of the instance chain providing the algebraic structure required for real matrix-vector multiplication; it adds no mathematical hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: NonUnitalNonAssocCommRing.toNonUnitalNonAssocRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: This forgets commutativity from a nonunital nonassociative commutative ring structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It continues the instance chain needed by Matrix.mulVec and adds no condition to the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: NonUnitalNonAssocRing.toNonUnitalNonAssocSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: This exposes the additive and multiplicative semiring operations underlying a nonunital nonassociative ring.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring Real instance required to define Matrix.mulVec.

dependency_coverage.name: NonUnitalNormedCommRing.toNonUnitalCommRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: This forgets the normed structure of a nonunital normed commutative ring and retains its nonunital commutative ring structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is an infrastructural step in obtaining the algebraic structure needed for real matrix-vector multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: NormedCommRing.toNonUnitalNormedCommRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: This forgets the multiplicative identity from a normed commutative ring while retaining its normed nonunital ring structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to Real, it begins the structure-forgetting chain that supplies Matrix.mulVec with the required semiring instance.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets a natural-number numeral in a type equipped with the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the exponent numeral 2 used in every squared entry or coordinate.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips Real with its additive commutative monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It permits the finite sums appearing in the matrix and vector norms.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips Real with its multiplicative monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies natural powers on Real, in particular the squares used in all norm formulas.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.normedCommRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips Real with its standard normed commutative ring structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real algebraic structures from which the structure required by Matrix.mulVec is obtained; it introduces no additional quantified assumption.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.sqrt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the nonnegative real square-root operation, implemented through the nonnegative reals; on a negative input it uses the input's nonnegative truncation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It takes the square root of each sum of squares. Those inputs are nonnegative, so these are the usual Frobenius and Euclidean norms.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a power operation Pow alpha beta, this constructs the corresponding homogeneous HPow alpha beta alpha operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It connects HPow.hPow on real bases and natural exponents to ordinary natural-number powers of real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets each natural-number numeral as that same natural number.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the exponent numeral 2 exactly the natural number two.

binders: n is an arbitrary natural number.
G is an arbitrary real n-by-n matrix, with entries G_ij indexed by i,j in Fin n.
a is an arbitrary real n-vector, indexed by Fin n.
epsilon is an arbitrary real number.
hypotheses: The Frobenius norm of G satisfies sqrt(sum_i sum_j G_ij^2) <= epsilon.
conclusions: The Euclidean norm of the matrix-vector product G a satisfies sqrt(sum_i (sum_j G_ij a_j)^2) <= epsilon * sqrt(sum_i a_i^2).
mathematical_definitions: ||G||_F := sqrt(sum_{i in Fin n} sum_{j in Fin n} G_ij^2).
(G a)_i := sum_{j in Fin n} G_ij a_j.
All sums, products, powers, square roots, and inequalities are exact operations on real numbers.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural number n, every real n-by-n matrix G, every real n-vector a, and every real number epsilon, if the Frobenius norm of G is at most epsilon, then the Euclidean norm of G a is at most epsilon times the Euclidean norm of a. Equivalently, ||G||_F <= epsilon implies ||G a||_2 <= epsilon ||a||_2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement concerns only finite-dimensional square matrices over the real numbers; it does not state a rectangular, complex, or infinite-dimensional version.
No assumption n > 0 is present. When n = 0, all relevant sums are empty and both norms are zero.
There is no explicit hypothesis epsilon >= 0. Since ||G||_F is nonnegative, the given hypothesis implies epsilon >= 0 whenever it is satisfiable; for epsilon < 0 the proposition is vacuous.
There is no restriction that a be nonzero, normalized, or otherwise special.
Epsilon need only be an upper bound for ||G||_F; it is not required to equal that norm.
The conclusion has the exact multiplicative constant 1: no additional dimension-dependent or approximation factor is present.
The proposition contains no existential witnesses and asserts no equality, lower bound, converse, optimality, or sharpness.
The proposition encodes exact real arithmetic only. It contains no floating-point format, rounding operation, computed approximation, algorithm, perturbation model, or error term.
